routes.reason: Source of GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.0 for the intrinsic-span, saturation, orthogonal-quotient and dual-lattice items. GN.0 is the lattice carrier layer and the route explicitly declines to reimplement the audited covolume material, which is the right line: the five library items already cite that carrier.

Source of GN.4 for the quantitative lattice-point counts (Lemmas 3.4–3.6, 3.18–3.24 and the S_{r,n} sums). GN.4 owns lattice-point/transference estimates and GN.1 owns successive minima, which is where the two Minkowski-second-theorem items are sent as planned; the reason names the ST.2 overlap and forbids duplicating it.

Source of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0 for the coefficient-family, sign-quotient and Euclidean-ordering items. These are families-and-measures statements about V_{d,n}(A) = a Euclidean ball of integral coefficient vectors, not isomorphism-weighted moduli counts, so ST.0 is the owner.

Source of ST.2 for the local-density product and its tail/shape transfer (§5.1, Lemmas 5.1–5.4). ST.2 owns infinite-local-condition uniformity and that is exactly what sigma(a;W) and its convergence require.
Source of ST.5 for the finite local-density moments and the gradient strata R^{(e)}(p^r) of Lemmas 5.5–5.7. These are source-scoped local statistics already in that layer's direction.

Source of HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.2 for the optional Brauer-vacuity comparison (Colliot-Thelene's appendix to Poonen-Voloch). RP.2 is the adelic/Brauer owner and the route is right that this is motivation rather than an input to the main theorem; the one planned item on everywhere-local solubility goes to the same stage.

Part II of HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions, title 'Heights, rational points and obstructions, Part II: random Fano hypersurfaces and least-point heights' — the prefix reproduces the parent's atlas title exactly, area 'arithmeticgeometry' is a galaxy id, and the brief is 237 words. RP.0-RP.6 plan height and obstruction foundations, not a density-one Hasse principle or the sharp typical least-point bound, so a Part II rather than a stage is right, and the reason distinguishes the separate SS23 random-fibration proposal by method.

Source of ST.4 for the single item on Bhargava's positive proportion of soluble plane cubics, used only for the (d,n)=(3,3) case of Corollary 1.2, where p.3 restricts the points to a coordinate hyperplane and so reduces cubic surfaces to plane cubic curves. ST.4 owns the genus-one Selmer-counting direction that supplies it.

notes: Accept. 129 items (120 missing, 5 library, 4 planned), every missing item routed exactly once across the eight routes, and check_paper.py passes. I reproduced the recorded hash of arXiv 2006.02356v1 (210c746b…) and re-extracted all 66 pages. All six library citations resolve at the Mathlib pin 082e2d3 with file and line: MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Homogeneous.lean:89), IsZLattice (ZLattice/Basic.lean:432), ZLattice.covolume, covolume_eq_measure_fundamentalDomain and covolume_div_covolume_eq_relIndex' (Covolume.lean:72, 84, 170) and LinearMap.BilinForm.dualSubmodule (BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean:37). All seven source-route stages and all four planned layer ids exist, the last being the designed GlobalQuadraticForms layer 5. Locators: of 72 name-and-page checks 61 land on exactly the page given, and I read every one of the other eleven — each is a proof that spans pages (Lemma 3.24 stated p.25 and proved p.26, Lemma 4.8 stated p.34 and proved to p.40, Lemma 5.7 stated p.56, Lemma 5.10 stated p.62, Proposition 4.1 stated p.26 and closed p.50), an external citation ([6, Lemma 3.3], not this paper's Lemma 3.3), or E19's locator naming both the statement's page and the three later places of use. Nothing needed correcting. All nineteen findings are printed as quoted and I checked each argument independently: E16's certificate recomputes exactly (30/173 = 0.173… below the printed 1/4, and a search over small integer pairs found no ratio below 1/8, so the proposed d=2 constant is safe); E8 fails at d=2, u=(1,1,0,…) with ||nu(u)||^2 = 3 < 4 = ||u||^{2d}; E17 follows from homogeneity of degree d−1 applied to x = x'/2; E2 and E4 are both counterexamples against definition (5.28), where I^loc asks only for a non-trivial real point, so X_0^d lies in it with every real zero singular and X_0^2+X_1^2+X_2^2 in four variables lies in it while a+t(b−a) never does; E5's assertion fails for the quartic t_1^2 t_2^2 and the proposed grid bound O(H_1H_2) returns exactly the printed (3.31); E1 is a genuine degree mismatch (M_{d−2,n} are monomials of degree d−2 by Definition 3.10 and L^{(x,y)}_{i,j,k} is linear), and the surrounding Psi_P construction already multiplies quadratics, which is the correction; E12 is right that 'a' is introduced as an arbitrary non-zero dual vector, so (3.16) and (3.18) bound ||a||; E14's 'max' contradicts the 'since Z ≥ s_2' of (3.31), and definition (3.23) bounds ||x||,||y|| by Z so the misprint costs nothing; E3 kills Lemma 3.19 at Delta = 1 because d_r(e_0) = 1, and Lemma 3.20 likewise for r ≥ 3; E6's ratio is unbounded exactly as described; E18's Lemma 4.7 does assume A ≥ B^{4/5} while (4.71) integrates over all smaller cutoffs; E19 is right that Poonen–Voloch count sup-norm boxes while this paper orders by Euclidean balls; E15's Barroero–Widmer constant does depend on the number of cones; E11's g lives modulo p^r; and E13 is unused by the paper's own statement on p.51. The version boundary of G1 stands and this review does not lift it: arXiv still lists only v1 and Crossref records no erratum or relation for 10.4007/annals.2023.197.3.3, so every verdict above is a verdict about v1. Nothing was corrected, rejected or deleted.
